concepts.title: Properties of Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: Rational numbers - numbers writable as a ratio of two integers with nonzero denominator - obey closure, commutativity and associativity under addition and multiplication; subtraction is closed too, while division fails closure because division by zero is undefined.
concepts.formula: sum = a + b stays rational for rational a, b
concepts.key_idea: Adding or multiplying rationals never leaves the family; dividing can, since zero has no inverse.
question_patterns: check whether subtraction of rational numbers is commutative
is division of rational numbers closed - justify with an example
verify the associative property of addition for three rationals
which operations are closed on rational numbers
show that addition of rational numbers is commutative
state the property that fails for division of rational numbers

solution_steps.explain: Choose two or three rational numbers to test the property.
Swap or regroup the operands and evaluate each side.
Equal results support the property; a counterexample refutes it.

concepts.title: Additive Inverse of a Rational Number
concepts.definition: The additive inverse of a rational number is the negative that cancels it: adding a number and its inverse gives zero, so -a/b is the additive inverse of a/b.
concepts.key_idea: a plus its negative equals zero: that negative is the additive inverse.
question_patterns: find the additive inverse of 3/7
what is the additive inverse of -5/9
which number added to 2/11 gives zero
verify that a rational number plus its additive inverse is zero
find the number to be added to -4/13 to get 0
what is the additive inverse of zero

solution_steps.explain: Changing the sign gives the additive inverse.

concepts.title: Multiplicative Inverse of a Rational Number
concepts.definition: The multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of a rational number is the fraction that multiplies it to give 1: the inverse of a/b is b/a, defined for every rational except zero.
concepts.key_idea: Flip the fraction to get the reciprocal; zero alone has no multiplicative inverse.
question_patterns: find the multiplicative inverse of 7/9
what is the reciprocal of -4/5
which number multiplied by 3/8 gives 1
why does zero have no multiplicative inverse
verify that a rational times its reciprocal is 1
find the reciprocal of 2 1/3 as a rational number

solution_steps.explain: Dividing 1 by the value flips the fraction.

concepts.title: Addition of Rational Numbers with Different Denominators
concepts.definition: To add rationals with unlike denominators, rewrite both over the product denominator and add the cross-multiplied numerators: a/b plus c/d equals (ad + cb) over bd, then reduce the result to lowest terms.
concepts.key_idea: Cross-multiply, add the numerators, and keep the product denominator.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh101.txt sections on operations (addition and subtraction)
question_patterns: add 2/3 and 3/5
find the sum of two rational numbers with different denominators
calculate 5/7 plus 1/2 and reduce to lowest terms
add the given rational numbers and simplify
what is the total of 3/4 and -1/6
subtract 2/9 from 5/6 using the cross method

solution_steps.explain: a*d plus c*b is the numerator over the common denominator bd.
The sum is num over b*d, reduced if possible.

concepts.title: Rational Numbers Between Two Given Numbers
concepts.definition: Between any two rational numbers lie infinitely many rationals; the simplest to find is the mean - half the sum of the two numbers - and repeating the process keeps producing fresh rationals between the originals.
concepts.key_idea: Average the endpoints to harvest a rational right between them.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh101.txt section 1.3 (rational numbers between two rational numbers)
question_patterns: find a rational number between 1/4 and 1/2
how many rational numbers lie between two given rationals
use the mean method to find three numbers between 2/5 and 3/5
find two rational numbers between -1 and 0
is the average of two rationals always between them - justify
insert five rational numbers between the given pair

solution_steps.explain: The mean lies midway, hence between the two numbers.

solution_template.explain: The additive inverse is the negative of the value.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What must be added to {value} to get 0?

solution_template.explain: Adding the negative cancels the number to zero.
1 divided by the value is its multiplicative inverse.

worked_examples.question_pattern: By what should {value} be multiplied to get the product 1?

solution_template.explain: The required multiplier is the reciprocal.
The sum is num over b*d.
The quotient is the combined fraction.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find a rational number between {low} and {high}.

solution_template.explain: The mean lies between the endpoints.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Using the mean method, insert a rational number between {low} and {high}.

solution_template.explain: Half the sum is the inserted rational.
